summary.short: From 1 January 2026, makes it a civil rights violation under the Illinois Human Rights Act for an employer to use artificial intelligence with a discriminatory effect on protected classes, to use zip codes as a proxy for protected classes, or to fail to notify employees of AI use.
summary.long: Public Act 103-0804 amends Sections 2-101 and 2-102 of the Illinois Human Rights Act. It adds definitions of "artificial intelligence" (a machine-based system that infers from its input how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments; it includes generative artificial intelligence) and of "generative artificial intelligence". It adds subdivision (L) to the list of employment civil rights violations: with respect to recruitment, hiring, promotion, renewal of employment, selection for training or apprenticeship, discharge, discipline, tenure, or terms, privileges or conditions of employment, it is a violation for an employer to use artificial intelligence that has the effect of subjecting employees to discrimination on the basis of protected classes under the Article, or to use zip codes as a proxy for protected classes. Failing to notify employees of such use of artificial intelligence is also a violation. The Department must adopt rules on implementation and enforcement, including when notice is required, its timing and its means. The restated definitions cover employers with one or more employees in Illinois during 20 or more calendar weeks, with exceptions. Procedures and remedies for civil rights violations are not stated in this Act.

evidence.quote: It is a civil rights violation: ... (L) Use of artificial intelligence.

"Artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. "Artificial intelligence" includes generative artificial intelligence.
"Generative artificial intelligence" means an automated computing system that, when prompted with human prompts, descriptions, or queries, can produce outputs that simulate human-produced content

notes: Only Sec. 2-101(M)-(N) and Sec. 2-102(L) are new (underlined in the official PDF); other restated subdivisions of 2-101 and 2-102 (e.g., the 30-day notice-to-show-cause procedure in 2-102(K)(2), which applies to violations of paragraph (1) of subdivision (K) only) are existing law and are not coded as obligations, thresholds or enforcement of this Act. Paragraph (L)(1) refers to 'employees', while the restated definition of 'employee' in 2-101(A) includes apprenticeship applicants but does not mention other job applicants; the text does not address this further. The zip-code clause in (L)(1) is a separate infinitive ('or to use zip codes as a proxy') and does not itself mention artificial intelligence. Left for the resolve stage: the identity of 'the Department' and the meaning of 'unlawful discrimination' and protected classes (defined elsewhere in the Illinois Human Rights Act, outside this text); the procedures and remedies for civil rights violations; the content and date of the Department's notice rules.
